morning: Morning. The streets are quiet before the shift whistle.
Early walk. It is the only time the city is not shouting.
day: Out for some air. The flat gets small.
Do not mind me, I am only between errands.
If you want a bargain, ask the exchange, not the street.
The orders on the terminals change daily. Check them.
evening: Home soon. The streets belong to the guard after dark.
Heat fades if you keep your head down. That is all the advice I have.

morning: On my way in. The shift does not wait.
Early start. Overtime pays, but not enough.
Mind the cart, I am carrying parts.
day: Lunch is short and the foreman is long.
Orders for the foundry go up on the terminal at the Row.
If you need parts, the exchange has them. If you need them cheap, ask nicely.
evening: Done for the day. Not done for the week.
My back says go home. My wallet says one more shift.

morning: First run of the day. Do not stand in the road.
Parcels for Valewood this morning. Bridge was clear.
day: Three cities, two bridges, one bicycle. You do the maths.
Package for a locked flat. They never answer the bell.
Road is quick if you keep to the left.
evening: Last parcel. Then I sleep for a week.
The checkpoints look in the hold as well as the cab. Declare what you carry.

morning: Quiet night. Keep it that way.
day: I keep the street clear. The checkpoints on the roads search on evidence, not suspicion.
Carry what your licence covers and we will never meet twice.
Locks are for honest people. A lockpick is for everyone else, and it leaves a mark on your name.
evening: Evening patrol. Stay in the light.
After dark the streets are ours. Go home.

morning: Long night. I'm heading home to sleep it off.
Is anything open for breakfast round here?
day: Just killing time before the evening.
My friends are late, as usual.
evening: We're meeting at the club later. The queue gets long after ten.
First round's on me tonight. Don't tell anyone.
The music starts at nine. Best night of the week.
Have you been to the place on the corner? The bartender knows everyone.
any: Evening. Or is it morning already?
Mind the doorman, he's in a mood tonight.
